head: split/authentication-only
title: Split rate limiting out of AutoAuth into independent AutoLimit
body:
AutoAuth now provides authentication and authorization without installing endpoint or IP rate limiting. Limiter consumers must opt into the independent AutoLimit library and provide an application-owned identity bridge.

Changes:
- Remove limiter annotations, aspect, service, IP filter, exception/resolver, identity interfaces, and dedicated tests.
- Remove limiter beans, filter-chain installation, and `autoauth.pre-auth-rate-limit`.
- Keep JWTs, keys, authorization/roles, bans, revocation, Swagger configuration, Redis, Caffeine, and authentication dependencies unchanged. No AutoLimit dependency is added.
- Move mixed limiter coverage into AutoLimit; retain authentication/configuration and 401/403 coverage here.
- Add [consumer migration instructions](https://github.com/AutoSprings/AutoAuth/blob/split/authentication-only/docs/migration-autolimit.md).

Source and companion:
- Based on the verified `separate-auth-limit` source at `d388ffd135fec8ab6307bdef9d9bcee067ee43fc`, including its CallerIdentity preparation commits. Those commits remain in this branch's normal ancestry.
- [AutoLimit implementation branch](https://github.com/AutoSprings/AutoLimit/tree/split/independent-library) contains the copied implementation/tests and the separate consuming example. The pre-existing local resolver test edits were carried into that repository.

Validation run locally with Java 21 / Gradle 9:
- ` .\gradlew.bat build `: PASS, 89 tests, zero failures/errors/skips.
- ` .\gradlew.bat dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath ` and `testRuntimeClasspath`: inspected; neither contains AutoLimit.
- Authentication-only MVC/security context tests run without AutoLimit; public/protected paths, real JWT authentication, roles, revocation, JWKS, CORS, and bean overrides pass.
- Built JAR inspected: no extracted limiter or identity classes.
- Companion consuming example build: PASS, 3 real-HTTP integration tests covering JWT user IDs/roles, quotas, one IP filter invocation per request, and early IP rejection before JWT validation.

Consumer migration:
Add AutoLimit only when needed, change limiter imports to `com.autolimit`, rename the exception resolver, move the property prefix to `autolimit`, and provide CallerIdentityResolver using AuthContext. Do not install the IP filter in the security chain; AutoLimit registers it in the servlet container before security.

Existing concern outside this split:
The unchanged springdoc 2.8.17 starter pulls Boot 3.5 components into the 3.2.4 baseline, causing full Boot startup to fail with mixed Spring Data versions. The consuming example excludes that optional Swagger UI dependency to validate auth/limiting on the existing baseline. Library dependency versions are not upgraded here.
